 This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail in Crime No.151/2022 of Bhadravathi New Town Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 306 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short).

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State and perused the material on record.
3.
Brief facts: - The marriage of deceased - Smitha was performed with the petitioner/accused No.1 on 30.04.2010.
While residing in her matrimonial home, she was being subjected to mental torture by her husband and parents NC: 2023:KHC:19034 in law.
Accused were picking up quarrel for petty reasons telling the deceased that her character is not good etc.
They were telling that no sufficient gold was given at the time of marriage and the marriage was not performed properly.
They were demanding two lakhs from her.
Petitioner was telling that he will give divorce to her and marry another girl.
In view of the physical and mental torture, she committed suicide by hanging in her matrimonial home on 21.11.2022.

4. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that for more than twelve years, the deceased and petitioner lived happily and in their wedlock, they have two children and there is not even a single complaint lodged against the petitioner alleging that he has demanded money or subjected the deceased to cruelty etc.
He submits that the petitioner is innocent and he is the only earning member of the family and in view of his detention, his aged parents and children are suffering.
He submits that the petitioner is ready and willing to furnish sufficient surety to ensure his presence before the trial Court.
Therefore, seeks to allow the petition.

sentences.text: 2 5. Learned High Court Government Pleader on the other hand has contended that on account of the physical and mental torture by the petitioner, the deceased has committed suicide and there are prima facie materials to show that the petitioner has abetted her to commit suicide.

He therefore,
seeks to reject the petition.
6. The complaint is lodged by the mother of the deceased against petitioner/accused No.1 and his parents.
The petitioner was arrested on 22.11.2022.

A perusal of the complaint averments goes to show that the marriage of CW.14 namely, brother of the deceased was fixed and in this connection,
the complainant, CW.14 and others had visited the house of accused No.1 to give the marriage invitation card.

At that time, accused No. 1 picked up quarrel with them saying that they have given a finger ring weighing 7 grams instead of 10 grams at the time of marriage and saying so he returned the new clothes given by them and told them that he will not send his wife for the marriage.

It is also alleged that on the date of incident, the accused had quarreled with the deceased on the ground that she did not prepare evening snacks for his father/accused No.2.
NC: 2023:KHC:19034 7.
The prosecution has to establish that the petitioner/accused No.1 has intentionally aided or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
The ingredients of the offences alleged have to be established in the course of trial.
Petitioner is in judicial custody since 22.11.2022.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Hence, by imposing necessary conditions, to ensure the presence of the petitioner before the trial Court, he can be enlarged on bail.

Accordingly, following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

The petitioner - Accused No.1 shall be enlarged on bail in Crime No.151/2022 of Bhadravathi New Town Police Station pending in C.C.No.1325/2023 on the file of IV Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Bhadravathi, Shivamogga subject to following conditions:
(i) Petitioner shall execute a personal bond in a sum of 1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the like sum to the NC: 2023:KHC:19034 satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
(ii) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Court if there is any change in the address.
(iii) Petitioner shall not tamper with the  prosecution witnesses/evidence  either directly or indirectly.
(iv) Petitioner shall not leave the Nagendra.
